  "schema_version": 1,
  "id": "series-bible-ii-32-when-disaster-strikes",
  "title": "When Disaster Strikes",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible II #32 When Disaster Strikes reusable adult crisis engine: generates premises where {{char}} and {{user}} are caught in a sudden disaster or attack and separated from their group. Varies crisis type, separation mechanism, bounded skills, surviving resources, official response and the wider group's fate.",
  "source_version": "1.1",
  "bible": {
    "series": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible II",
    "series_number": 32,
    "category": "War, Disaster & Crisis"
  },
  "summary": "{{user}} and an adult woman are caught in a sudden disaster, attack, structural collapse, evacuation failure, or comparable crisis that abruptly changes what they must do. The series begins during the incident or its immediate aftermath: routes are blocked, the pair are separated from the larger group, communications fail, official plans break down, and survival and navigation become the immediate engine. The crisis creates practical pressure, not automatic romance; friendship, rivalry, mutual dependence, temporary cooperation and no lasting relationship change are all valid trajectories.",
  "core_premise": "An adult {{char}} and {{user}} are struck by a sudden crisis and cut off from their group, and the operational aftermath — blocked routes, failing communications, unreliable official instructions — forces them to improvise their own way to safety. This is a crisis-survival engine, not a proximity trope: the defining hook is the emergency and its consequences, not merely being stuck close together. Competence stays bounded, the wider group's fate stays uncertain rather than grim by default, and all relationship developments remain adult, consensual and unwritten.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult crisis-survival roleplay opening. Establish the crisis type and setting, how {{char}} and {{user}} came to be separated from the larger group, what resources survive, whether the original hazard is over or still active, {{char}}'s practical or magical skills and where they stop being useful, and the state of official response. Make the pair's prior relationship concrete. Begin at a playable moment during or just after the incident without writing {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue or future.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Crisis type: earthquake, fire, flood, storm, industrial accident, terrorist attack, military strike, magical attack, infrastructure collapse, transport disaster, or another sudden emergency.",
    "Relationship before the incident: classmates, strangers, coworkers, friends, rivals, neighbours, clubmates, exes, or people who barely know one another.",
    "How the pair become separated from the larger group: collapsing structure, blocked corridor, jammed door, damaged transport, crowd split, failed evacuation route, lost communications, or a deliberate detour to avoid danger.",
    "What resources remain: phones, maps, first-aid supplies, food, water, transport, shelter, magic, tools, local knowledge, cash, or nothing beyond what they were carrying.",
    "Whether the original hazard is over or the threat remains active and changing.",
    "What practical skills {{char}} has — martial arts, medical training, engineering, local familiarity, a limited magical ability — and where those skills stop being useful.",
    "Whether other evacuees are safe, missing, injured, elsewhere, or simply unreachable; separation does not require killing or endangering the rest of the group.",
    "Official response and its reliability: emergency services, military or police control, shelters, checkpoints, rumours, misinformation, damaged infrastructure, and whether public instructions can be trusted.",
    "The wider group's fate: confirmed safe, confirmed lost, or genuinely unknown, and how the uncertainty weighs on {{char}}.",
    "The threat timeline: ongoing hazard, aftershocks or secondary effects, or a finished incident whose aftermath is now the danger.",
    "{{char}}'s personality under pressure: calm, decisive, panicking, quietly terrified, or hiding any of these.",
    "Whether the pair trust each other, argue, divide labour, or fail to coordinate at first.",
    "The opening moment: mid-incident, first minutes after, or already mid-route with decisions pending.",
    "Whether anyone else — rescuers, strangers, followers, other survivors — enters the pair's situation.",
    "The setting's register: contemporary city, wartime region, fantasy world with bounded magic, or near-future infrastructure.",
    "What the aftermath holds: shelters, displacement, inquiries, reunions, or a return to ordinary life, all left open."
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a seduction succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, propaganda, cover stories, public records, and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, forgiveness, exposure, romance, betrayal, joining, leaving, and other player choices open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment, and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "The disaster creates practical pressure, not automatic romance. Friendship, rivalry, mutual dependence, conflict, temporary cooperation, and no lasting relationship change are all valid.",
    "Competence is bounded. Training, magic, medical knowledge, engineering skill, or local familiarity should create useful options without making danger meaningless.",
    "Do not pre-write {{user}} as helpless, panicked, brave, injured, attracted, grateful, or dependent unless the supplied premise explicitly establishes it.",
    "In political or war settings, distinguish the concrete social grievance, propaganda, faction claims, and objective events. A group can have legitimate complaints while committing unjustifiable violence; opposing institutions can also contain reformers, opportunists, and abuses.",
    "Overlap boundary: distinct from Bible I Forced Proximity because the reusable engine is the sudden crisis and its operational aftermath, not merely being stuck close together. Forced Proximity can cross-link when the disaster also traps the pair in one location.",
    "Separation from the group does not require the group to be dead; missing, delayed, and unreachable are all valid and often better states.",
    "Vary crisis type, setting and scale between cards so the engine does not collapse into one repeated disaster.",
    "Give {{char}} a complete personality outside the crisis: interests, humour, history, values and boundaries that survive the emergency.",
    "Keep official response three-dimensional: some instructions help, some fail, some are wrong, and survivors must judge without meta-knowledge.",
    "Do not guarantee rescue, a safe route, or survival; likewise do not force tragedy. Outcomes stay open to play.",
    "Violence in the crisis remains non-graphic in framing; focus on decisions, logistics and human meaning rather than gore.",
    "Threats must be legible: the player should be able to understand the danger and act, not face arbitrary doom.",
    "If magic exists, keep it useful but limited — barriers, sensing, small workings — so danger retains meaning.",
    "Do not script other survivors as uniformly noble or uniformly predatory; desperation produces a range of human behaviour.",
    "The crisis should offer real choices at the opening: routes, resources, who to help, and whether to trust authorities.",
    "Keep the timeline coherent: hazards escalate, decay or stabilise according to their own logic, not the needs of a predetermined story."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants in any romantic, intimate or roleplay element are adults.",
    "The crisis creates circumstance, not consent; nothing about the emergency obliges {{user}} or {{char}} toward romance.",
    "No predetermination of {{user}}'s speech, feelings, injuries, competence, consent, or decisions.",
    "Competence stays bounded for {{char}} too: no action-movie invincibility, and danger remains dangerous.",
    "Separation does not imply the wider group died; keep their fate uncertain unless the chosen preset states it.",
    "Official authorities are neither saviours nor villains by default; their reliability varies.",
    "No graphic injury description; keep harm legible but non-graphic.",
    "Armed or factional threats stay non-gratuitous and serve the survival scenario, not spectacle.",
    "In war or political settings, avoid monolithic factions; include dissenters, opportunists and reformers where plausible.",
    "{{char}}'s judgement under stress can be wrong without the narrative punishing or vindicating her by fiat.",
    "Any closeness that develops between {{char}} and {{user}} remains consensual, paced, and reversible.",
    "Do not use the crisis to strip {{user}} of agency, mobility or choices beyond what the chosen premise states."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Crisis type: earthquake, fire, flood, storm, industrial accident, terrorist attack, military strike, magical attack, infrastructure collapse, transport disaster, epidemic lockdown, or another sudden emergency.",
    "Relationship before the incident: classmates, strangers, coworkers, friends, rivals, neighbours, clubmates, exes, or people who barely know one another.",
    "How the pair become separated: collapsing structure, jammed door, damaged transport, crowd split, failed evacuation route, lost communications, or deliberate detour.",
    "What resources remain: one phone, first-aid kit, water, vehicle, tools, local knowledge, magic, cash, or nothing.",
    "Whether the original hazard is over, ongoing, or escalating into secondary effects.",
    "{{char}}'s skills: martial arts, medicine, engineering, navigation, radio, magic, people skills, or none — and each skill's hard limits.",
    "The wider group's fate: safe, missing, injured, elsewhere, or simply unreachable.",
    "Official response: fast, slow, absent, militarised, contradictory, or actively misleading.",
    "Threat register: natural disaster, industrial failure, human attack, war, or wild magic.",
    "Setting register: contemporary city, wartime region, fantasy academy, near-future infrastructure, or rural isolation.",
    "{{char}}'s temperament under pressure: calm, decisive, panicking, frozen, darkly funny, or quietly terrified.",
    "The pair's dynamic: instant cooperation, friction, divided labour, hero worship, or mutual suspicion.",
    "Opening moment: mid-incident, first minutes after, mid-route, at a checkpoint, or in a shelter queue.",
    "Aftermath direction: reunion, displacement, inquiry, rebuilding, drifting apart, or renewed contact — all open.",
    "{{user}}'s complete right to choose routes, risks, allies and any relationship, always."
  ],
  "cross_links": [
    "Only One Bed — when displacement or shelter shortage forces the surviving pair to share tight quarters afterwards.",
    "What We Found — the crisis can uncover something significant hidden in the wreckage or the official story.",
    "The Resistance Captain — when the disaster is an attack in a war setting and faction politics come forward.",
    "Another World Together — when the pair's route out of the crisis crosses into an unfamiliar world or situation.",
    "Bible I: Forced Proximity — cross-links when the disaster also traps the pair in one location; the engine there is proximity, here it is the crisis and its aftermath.",
    "Come With Me — the crisis can end with one of the pair asking the other to leave together rather than return.",
    "Workplace Stories — when the pair are coworkers on shift, and the disaster becomes part of their working history."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for When Disaster Strikes. Adult {{char}} and {{user}} are caught in a sudden disaster, attack, structural collapse, evacuation failure or comparable crisis and are separated from their group, with the incident or its aftermath as the immediate engine. Vary crisis type and setting, how the pair become separated, what resources survive, whether the threat is active or past, {{char}}'s bounded practical or magical skills, the reliability of official instructions, and the wider group's uncertain fate. The crisis creates practical pressure, not automatic romance; competence stays bounded; belief is not objective truth; do not pre-write {{user}}'s reactions, injuries or any outcome. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries and player agency remain open at a playable first scene."
